title: Godforsaken Scavengers - When Art and Theme Don't Win Me Over
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wX47G7oi_Z4

Daniel (@dungeondive) frames this as the mirror image of his Fire of Eidolon review. There, a strong theme won him over; here, a cool theme and genuinely great art combine and still don't. Godforsaken Scavengers is one of the rare occasions he'll do a straight negative review, and he gets to the verdict early: a hard pass.

The game is a press-your-luck survival crawl. Seven areas, each with a value you must feed by flipping cards off scavenge piles until you have enough — or until a peril card busts your turn and hands you an affliction. Six afflictions ends the game. You start with one card in hand, which he notes may well be the most you ever hold. His objection isn't that the mechanism is broken but that there's nothing behind it: press-your-luck should generate tension, and DungeonQuest manages it because theme and art pour through the mechanism. Here he feels nothing.

The back half turns to vintage science fiction paperbacks, including books stamped by Raymond C. Jones — a Seattle collector whose library went to Half Price Books, and whose volumes Daniel buys to reassemble. There's Cordwainer Smith and the Instrumentality of Mankind, Simak's City, Leigh Brackett, and a recommended space opera trio.

----

Can great art and a strong theme rescue a game whose core mechanism leaves you cold?
